# Intake Brief — Validate all card text (CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0)

## Problem statement

The integer-economy migration (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled coin/reputation
**data** ×100 but only partially updated the **card text**. Business,
community-space, upgrade, and staff `description` fields were scaled, but every
event `effect` field was left at its pre-migration display-scale value (e.g.
`evt-festival` reads `+2 coins` while its `coinDelta` is `200`), and
`evt-shopping-spree` still shows a fractional `+2.5 coins` (data `250`).
Players therefore read card text that disagrees with the amount the engine
actually applies, with the activity log, and with the raw-integer HUD. The
same stale values also remain in every other player-visible surface that
repeats card coin/reputation amounts — card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy,
staff-skill descriptions, and the `docs/main-street/*` reference material.

## Users

- **Player** — needs each card's text to state the same coin/reputation amount
  that will actually be applied, so purchase/play decisions are informed.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs `card-data.csv` text and data columns to
  agree so balancing is based on accurate descriptions.
- **Developer / QA** — needs a durable check that catches future card-text/data
  drift instead of relying on manual review.

### User stories

- As a player, when I read an event card's effect text I see the same
  coin/reputation amount that the game applies and that the activity log shows.
- As a designer, I can trust that every card description matches its
  `card-data.csv` values without mental ×100 conversion.
- As a developer, a failing check tells me exactly which card's text no longer
  matches its data.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Every player-visible card-text surface is ×100-consistent with card
   data.** Every numeric coin/reputation mention in card text equals the
   corresponding data column (`coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`,
   `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `reputationBonus`, `incomeBonus`,
   staff-skill magnitudes) under the documented ×100 scale. The audited
   surfaces are: the `card-data.csv` `description` and `effect` columns;
   card-face SVG text (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and committed SVG
   artifacts); tooltips (`MainStreetFormatting.ts`); tutorial copy
   (`TutorialFlow.ts`, `i18n/tutorial-en.ts`); staff-skill descriptions
   (`MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`); and the `docs/main-street/*` reference
   material. All event `effect` texts are scaled (e.g. `evt-festival`
   `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`); `evt-shopping-spree` `+2.5 coins` →
   `+250 coins`. No fractional coin/reputation value remains in any
   player-visible card text.
2. **Non-coin/reputation numbers are unchanged.** Percentages (`45%`, `90%`,
   `120%`), durations (`3 turns`), hand-slot counts, levels, and the
   `{SYNERGY_RATE}` token are out of scope and verified unchanged.
3. **Automated regression test guards against drift.** An automated unit test
   parses every card's text coin/reputation mentions and asserts they match the
   card's data columns under the documented ×100 scale, failing with a message
   that identifies the offending card. The test must run in the `unit` profile
   and fail if a future edit desynchronises card text from card data.
4. **Tests and artifacts updated.** Existing test expectations that reference
   old text values are updated; committed card SVG artifacts are regenerated to
   match the corrected text; `npm run build` and the unit test profile pass.
5. **Documentation updated.** Every doc carrying stale fractional card values
   (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
   identified during implementation) is revised to the integer scale; code
   comments describing the old scale (e.g. the `{bonus}` example `+2 coins` in
   `TutorialFlow.ts`) are corrected. All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Text is corrected to match data; data
  values are not changed to match text.
- **Only coin/reputation amounts scale.** Percentage, rate, duration, and count
  values are untouched; `{SYNERGY_RATE}` stays a rate token resolved at render
  time.
- **Cover every player-visible surface (producer-confirmed).** Card-face SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs are all in scope,
  not just the CSV `description`/`effect` columns.
- **Automated tests required (producer-confirmed).** The regression guard is an
  automated unit test, not a manual checklist.
- **No rebalancing.** Apply text-only ×100 corrections; any balance change is a
  separate work item.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `card-data.csv` business/community-space/upgrade/staff `description` fields
  were scaled ×100 by CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6.
- Every event `effect` field retains its pre-migration value (small integers),
  while `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` were scaled ×100 — e.g. `evt-festival`
  `effect: "+2 coins to all Culture businesses and +1 reputation."`,
  `coinDelta: 200`, `reputationDelta: 100`.
- `evt-shopping-spree` is the only card with a fractional value in text:
  `"+2.5 coins to all Commerce businesses."` (`coinDelta: 250`).
- The HUD renders raw integers (`Coins: 1000`); the activity log renders raw
  integers via `describeEventEffects` (`+200 coins`); SpecificSynergy event
  tooltips show only the (small) `effect` text, so the mismatch is visible to
  players.
- `TutorialFlow.ts` resolves `{bonus}` from `coinDelta` (`+${coinDelta} coins`
  → `+200 coins`) but its doc comment still says `e.g. '+2 coins'`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and several other `docs/main-street/*`
  files, including `specialization-skills.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, and `prd-multi-use-card-economy.md`)
  still use fractional values such as `+0.4/turn` and `0.25 coins/turn`.
- No automated test currently compares card text amounts against card data;
  existing card tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
  `card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
  `csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic fixtures.

## Desired change

Audit every player-visible card-text source — CSV text, card-face SVGs,
tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs — scale all
coin/reputation amounts to match the integer data (×100), remove the last
fractional value, add an automated regression test so text/data drift is caught
automatically, and refresh stale docs and comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — scale every event `effect` coin/rep
  amount ×100 and fix the `evt-shopping-spree` fractional value; check remaining
  `description` fields.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — tooltip rendering of
  `effect`/`description`; confirm text/data consistency.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face
  text; confirm integer rendering and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill
  descriptions; verify already-scaled values.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` doc comment and any
  tutorial card-value copy.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — tutorial copy referencing
  card coin/reputation values.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip coin/rep
  values and card detail lines.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — committed card-face SVG
  artifacts; regenerate after text corrections.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
  with stale fractions — update to the integer scale.
- `tests/main-street/**` — new automated card-text/data consistency test plus
  updated expectations.

## Related work

- **Potentially related docs**
  - `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — canonical card text/data source.
  - `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — card catalogue with stale fractional values.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — card tooltip text builder.
  - `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face SVG text.
  - `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` interpolation and stale comment.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill descriptions.
- **Potentially related work items**
  - `Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6)` —
    completed; the migration whose text updates this item validates.
  - `Dynamic synergy bonus text on business cards (difficulty-aware percentage, Option B) (CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4)` —
    completed; dynamic card text rendering.
  - `Synergy bonus on business cards (CG-0MRXYHNHB006F0U9)` — completed;
    synergy text semantics.
  - `In main street log should show total effects (CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ)` —
    completed; log integer deltas that already disagree with event text.
  - `Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT)` —
    completed; tutorial copy review precedent.
  - `Fix card rendering, UI overlay, and formatting tests (CG-0MTKLQ1P40091YTH)` —
    completed; card rendering/formatting tests.
  - `Main Street Game over dialog is not showing text (CG-0MQ2IL40S0060FUG)` —
    completed; card/dialog text rendering precedent.
  - `Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7)` —
    completed; card-economy semantics behind the coin/rep values.
  - `Docs: tutorial-localization + README updates (CG-0MSLXJ1OK004LJKU)` —
    completed; tutorial/doc text-update precedent.

> **Automated related-work report:** `/skill:find-related` was run and inserted
> a report into the work item. Its findings are folded into the list above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: event `effect` scaling direction (confirmed ×100).** Producer
  confirmed event effect text scales ×100 to match `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`,
  consistent with the already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer
  HUD/log. The regression test encodes this.
- **Risk: natural-language parsing fragility.** Comparing text amounts to data
  columns requires parsing prose. Mitigation: constrain the test to well-formed
  `[+-]?N coins?` / `[+-]?N reputation` patterns and/or an explicit per-card
  expected-value map, with a clear failure message naming the card.
- **Risk: scope creep into rebalancing.** Mitigation: apply only ×100 text
  corrections; file a separate balance work item for any value change.
- **Risk: missed text sources.** Coin/reputation copy lives in CSV text, SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial strings, staff skills, and docs. Mitigation: grep the repo
  for fractional coin/rep patterns and for the `effect`/`description` columns,
  and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- **Risk: expanded scope increases effort.** Producer confirmed "cover
  everything" and automated tests, which widens the surface beyond the CSV and
  raises the estimate. Mitigation: effort/risk re-estimated after the scope
  confirmation.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** scope covers every player-visible surface that
  repeats card coin/reputation amounts (CSV text, SVGs, tooltips, tutorial
  copy, staff skills, docs); percentages, durations, and counts are out of
  scope.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** the regression guard is an automated unit test.
- **Assumption:** documentation updates cover the docs carrying stale card
  coin/reputation values; unrelated doc drift is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

An initial brief was drafted from the seed context, then three clarifying
questions were put to the producer and answered (2026-09-24, interactive
reply). The brief has been updated to the confirmed answers.

- **Q: Should event `effect` text be scaled ×100 to match
  `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` (e.g. `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`)?** —
  **Answer (producer): yes.** Source: interactive reply; consistent with the
  already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer HUD/log. Research:
  `git show 192943c9` showed the migration scaled descriptions but not the
  event `effect` column; `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` and
  `MainStreetStateLog.ts` render raw integers.
- **Q: Is "all card text" limited to the `card-data.csv` `description`/`effect`
  columns, or should it cover tooltips/SVGs/tutorial copy/docs too?** —
  **Answer (producer): cover everything.** Source: interactive reply. The brief
  now scopes card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions,
  and `docs/main-street/*`.
- **Q: Is an automated regression test the expected way to "ensure" ongoing
  correctness, or is a one-time audit-and-fix sufficient?** —
  **Answer (producer): automated tests.** Source: interactive reply. AC3 is now
  a required automated unit test rather than a manual checklist.

**Research summary:** `wl show CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 --json` established the
migration contract (CSV ×100, integer-only UI). `git show 192943c9` confirmed
the migration scaled business/community/staff/upgrade descriptions but did not
touch the event `effect` column. A CSV parse of all 173 rows found exactly one
remaining fractional text value (`evt-shopping-spree`, `+2.5 coins` vs
`coinDelta=250`) and showed every event `effect` still at display scale
(e.g. `evt-festival` `+2 coins` vs `coinDelta=200`). `MainStreetFormatting.ts`,
`MainStreetStateLog.ts` (`describeEventEffects`), `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`,
`TutorialFlow.ts`, and `MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` were inspected to map the
text sources and confirm the HUD/log render raw integers. `docs/main-street/*`
was grepped and found to retain fractional values in `card-catalog.md` and
several other files. Existing tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
`card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
`csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic data and contain no card-text/data
consistency guard. The producer's three answers (×100 direction, cover
everything, automated tests) were applied to the problem statement, AC1/AC3/AC5,
constraints, and risks.

# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).

# Ensure every Main Street card has a dedicated 64×64 sprite

## Goal

As a player, every Main Street card shows distinct, recognisable art in its 64×64 left-art zone — no card falls back to the generic `Fallback` sprite in the market, hand, or street.

## Context

discovered-from:CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN

The 64×64 left-art redesign (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN, commit 38cf1f08) embeds a 64×64 sprite PNG into every card face and resolves it by card name via `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` (generated by `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`), falling back to the `Fallback` sprite when no dedicated sprite exists.

Today only 63 sprites exist for the 171 card templates in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`, so ~108 cards render the same generic `Fallback` art. The gaps:

- **Upgrade cards (39)** — names like `Upgrade to Patisserie`; many have a `targetBusiness` that does resolve to a sprite (e.g. `Diner`, `Hardware Store`, `Boutique`), so at minimum upgrades can inherit their target's art.
- **Staff cards (25)** — no sprites (`Assistant`, `Chef`, `Security Guard`, …).
- **Event cards (~44)** — no sprites (`Rainy Day`, `Block Party`, `Tax Audit`, …).

## Proposed approach

Decide the art strategy per family (to confirm during intake/plan):

1. **Upgrades** — derive art from `targetBusiness` (or an explicit override when `targetBusiness` is empty), so each upgrade shows the business it enhances.
2. **Staff** — add role/family sprites or a small set of shared staff art.
3. **Events** — add per-event sprites or a documented category mapping (e.g. incident vs opportunity, festival vs economic).

Then extend the resolver and/or art map accordingly, keeping `Fallback` only as a genuine last resort.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every card in `card-data.csv` resolves via `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite (any documented mapping/alias counts).
2. Upgrade cards resolve to a sprite derived from their `targetBusiness` (or a documented explicit override); no upgrade shows generic `Fallback` art.
3. Staff cards each resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card shows generic `Fallback` art.
4. Event cards each resolve to dedicated or category-mapped art; no event card shows generic `Fallback` art.
5. A regression test asserts AC 1–4 (a drift guard over `card-data.csv`), and `Fallback` remains in the map/resolver for genuinely-unknown/future cards.
6. Docs (`docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`, `public/assets/CREDITS.md`) document the mapping rules and any new art's licence/attribution.
7. `npm run build` is green and the unit test suite passes.

## Risks / notes

- **Art strategy is a design decision** — unique art for 108 cards is a large asset effort; reuse/mapping (especially upgrades → target business) may be the pragmatic first step. Confirm scope with the producer.

# Prune 7 stale local branches that block the ship Step 1 unmerged-branches gate

## Problem statement

The `ship` skill's Step 1 gate (`scripts/check-unmerged-branches.js`) lists every local branch not merged into `dev` and aborts the release (exit 3) unless `--skip-checks` is passed. Seven stale local branches from the herdr implement workflow currently fail this gate, so the TCE v0.1.17 dev→main release had to be run with `--skip-checks` (all other gates were verified manually). `git branch --no-merged dev` currently reports **eight** refs — the seven below plus the protected `worklog/data`, which the gate filters out.

These branches share an old merge-base (`567ae2d4`) and diverge from `dev` by 360–430 files. Merging them would produce hundreds of conflicts, so the desired outcome is safe local-ref removal after per-branch verification — **not** merging.

## Users

- **Release operator / producer (primary)** — needs the ship Step 1 gate to pass without `--skip-checks` so releases are trustworthy and repeatable.
  *As a release operator, I want `git branch --no-merged dev` to list no stale branches so that `ship` Step 1 passes without bypasses.*
- **Engine maintainer (secondary)** — needs confidence that no unmerged work is silently discarded.
  *As a maintainer, I want each branch triaged against `dev` so that I can see exactly which commits are already represented and which are not.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the seven branches is triaged with `git cherry dev <branch>` (patch-id); the per-branch result (represented vs unrepresented commits) is recorded.
2. Branches whose content is fully represented on `dev` are deleted (local refs); any worktree holding a checked-out branch is removed first (`git worktree remove`, then `git branch -D`).
3. Any branch carrying commits NOT represented on `dev` is surfaced to the producer with the commit SHAs and subjects **before** deletion. No unreviewed work is discarded; deletion of such branches proceeds only on explicit producer approval (or after a documented backup ref/tag is created).
4. After cleanup, `git branch --no-merged dev` lists only protected refs (`worklog/data`), and `check-unmerged-branches.js` reports no unmerged branches (ship Step 1 passes without `--skip-checks`).
5. The main checkout and remaining worktrees are left clean; no unrelated worktrees or branches are removed.
6. Findings (per-branch triage table, deletion log, producer approvals) are recorded as a comment on this item.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (Branch pruning is expected to require no documentation change; confirm and record this explicitly.)
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (Branch pruning changes no tracked source, so the practical validation proxy is `npm run build` plus `npm test -- --project unit`.)

## Existing state (intake evidence, 2026-09-26)

`git branch --no-merged dev` → 8 refs: the 7 below + protected `worklog/data`.

Patch-id triage (`git cherry dev <branch>`; `+` = commit unrepresented on `dev`, `-` = represented):

| Branch | HEAD | On origin? | Worktree? | Patch-id verdict | Representative unrepresented commits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fix-bank-hint-tutorial` | `8ffdae34` | yes | no | unrepresented | `8ffdae34` do not fire banking hint during tutorial |
| `revert-fix` | `c8499907` | no | `/tmp/wl-revert` | unrepresented | `c8499907` track scheduled-prompts.json |
| `wl-CG-0MTIILIBQ009J49F-prd-m3-scope-note-tests-build` | `f426ffd7` | no | no | unrepresented | `f426ffd7` Implementation complete |
| `wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566-add-week-year-to-mainstreetstate-random` | `f9ea09b5` | yes | no | **fully represented** | none — `f9ea09b5` has a `-` patch-id match |
| `wl-CG-0MU9PKH5300114KR-run-full-audit-and-produce-test-suite-re` | `9ed86341` | no | no | unrepresented | `9ed86341`, `9e792ac3`, `7a204687`, `8c3d12f1`, `f426ffd7` |
| `wl-CG-0MU9PNH4Y009BCJQ-author-reproducible-test-review-skill` | `a3ebf2c0` | no | no | unrepresented | `a3ebf2c0`, `9ed86341`, `9e792ac3`, `7a204687`, `8c3d12f1`, `f426ffd7` |
| `wl-CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU-update-project-documentation-to-referenc` | `d76ab851` | no | `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU-…` | unrepresented | `d76ab851`, `a3ebf2c0`, `9ed86341`, `9e792ac3`, `7a204687`, `8c3d12f1`, `f426ffd7` |

**Correction to the original premise.** The original brief assumed all branches' work "already landed on dev via other paths". Patch-id evidence shows this is true for only **one** branch (`wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566…`). The other six each carry at least one commit with no patch-id equivalent on `dev`, and five of those six have **no `origin` counterpart** — so their commits are unrecoverable after local-ref deletion (beyond the local reflog until gc). This makes AC3 the critical safety gate.

## Desired change

- Delete the local refs proven fully represented on `dev`.
- For the remaining branches, obtain producer approval (or create a backup ref/tag) before deleting, after presenting the unrepresented commits.
- Remove now-unused worktrees that pin the branches.
- Confirm the ship Step 1 gate passes without `--skip-checks`.

## Constraints

- Never delete branches without the AC1 triage and, where required, AC3 producer approval.
- Keep the operation fully reversible where the work is not on `origin`: prefer `git tag backup/<branch> <sha>` (tags do **not** trip `git branch --no-merged`) or `refs/archive/*` over a backup *branch*, which would itself remain in the gate output.
- Do not touch `worklog/data` or other protected refs.
- Do not delete or stash unrelated worktrees; the repo has many active `wl-*` worktrees that must be preserved.
- `revert-fix` is checked out in `/tmp/wl-revert`; its worktree must be removed before the branch ref.
- `git branch -d` will refuse to delete unmerged branches; use `-D` only after AC3 approval, or delete then recreate as a backup tag.

## Key Files (predicted)

- No source files change. Relevant artefacts:
  - `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/check-unmerged-branches.js` — the gate whose output defines success.
  - `.git/refs/heads/*` — the local refs removed.
  - `.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU-update-project-documentation-to-referenc/` and `/tmp/wl-revert` — worktrees to remove before their branches.

## Related work

- Release that surfaced the issue: `CG-0MUDA0CLC007G6F7` (Release v0.1.17: promote dev to main).
- Ship-skill scoping gap (SorraAgents repo, not resolvable here): `SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H`.
- Content WIP referenced by unrepresented commits: `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58` (chain cards), `CG-0MTIILIBQ009J49F`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (high):** deleting one of the five non-origin branches discards commits with no other reachable ref. Mitigation: AC3 producer approval + backup tag/archive ref.
- **Risk (medium):** `fix-bank-hint-tutorial` and `wl-CG-0MTTA73RS007N566…` exist on `origin`, so local deletion is recoverable; their stale origin branches remain and may yet trip other tooling. Out of scope here; note as a follow-up.
- **Assumption:** the seven branches are herdr-workflow artefacts, not live feature work. Partially verified per AC1 (only 1 fully represented); the remainder require the AC3 handoff.
- **Scope-creep risk:** pruning the many other stale `wl-*` branches, origin branches, or worktrees is **not** in scope; capture as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (agent, intake): "For the six branches carrying commits not represented on `dev` (five with no `origin` counterpart), what is the approved disposal policy?"
  - Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer.
  - Options: (a) archive the commit SHAs/subjects in this item, then delete all seven; (b) create `backup/<branch>` **tags** (or `refs/archive/*`) for the unrepresented branches, then delete all seven; (c) delete only the fully-represented branch and keep the other six; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (b) — backup tags for the five non-origin branches are cheap and fully reversible, they do not appear in `git branch --no-merged`, and they let all seven local branches be deleted so the ship Step 1 gate passes.
  - Answer: _pending producer response_.

# Intake Brief: Beleaguered Castle — cards cannot be selected to move them (CG-0MUHKD7S8007EEAC)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> Fix a reproducible card-selection defect in Beleaguered Castle: the first click immediately after the deal completes is silently dropped because newly registered top cards are not yet hit-testable, and harden selection feedback so a click always produces visible, reliable selection regardless of renderer.

## Problem Statement

Operators report that in Beleaguered Castle they "cannot select any cards to move them". Investigation confirms at least one reproducible selection defect — the first click after the deal animation completes is ignored — plus two aggravating factors (no visible selection highlight under the Canvas renderer, and only the top card of each column being interactive). The result is that a player's click can appear to do nothing, making the game feel unresponsive or unplayable.

## Users

- **Solitaire player:** Wants to click a card and immediately see it selected, then click a destination to move it, without having to click twice or guess whether the click registered.
  - *"As a player, I want my first click on a card after the deal to select it, so the game feels responsive and I can plan moves confidently."*
- **QA / playtester:** Needs deterministic, reproducible interaction behaviour so selection bugs can be captured in browser tests and not recur.
  - *"As a tester, I want a browser regression test that fails if the first post-deal click is dropped, so this class of bug is caught automatically."*
- **Engine developer:** Wants the fix to live in the shared interaction layer (`src/ui/dragDrop.ts` / `HandView`) where the registration race originates, rather than as a game-local workaround.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want newly registered draggables to be hit-testable immediately, so every game using the shared module benefits."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **First post-deal click always selects:** In the natural (non-reduced-motion) boot flow — choose variant → deal completes → immediate first click on a tableau top card — the column is selected on the very first click, 100% of runs (no dropped click, no retry required). Verified by a new browser test that repeats the sequence across multiple boots/seeds.
2. **Selection is visibly indicated in all renderers:** A selected top card shows a persistent, distinct highlight under both WebGL and Canvas renderers (BC currently uses raw `setTint()`, which is a no-op in Phaser 4 Canvas; the shared HandView Canvas-compatible tint-overlay approach must be used or equivalent).
3. **End-to-end click-to-move works from a clean natural boot:** From a fresh natural boot, selecting a top card and then clicking a legal destination (foundation or tableau column) executes exactly one undoable move, with the highlight and selection state clearing/reset appropriately.
4. **Double-click / same-card deselect unaffected:** Clicking an already-selected card deselects it, and clicking a different valid source re-selects, preserving the documented click-to-move contract.
5. **Regression tests:** New browser test(s) under `tests/beleaguered-castle/` cover the first-click and click-to-move flows in the natural boot path; the existing drag/click coexistence tests continue to pass.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `help-content.json` if the interaction contract changes, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve dual-input:** Both drag-and-drop and click-to-move must continue to work simultaneously; the click-vs-drag threshold (`dragDistanceThreshold`) behaviour must be preserved.
- **No behavioural regression for other games:** Any change to the shared drag-drop module (`src/ui/dragDrop.ts`) or `HandView` must not break Main Street, Golf, Coloretto, the Gym, or other consumers. Prefer a fix at the shared layer that is additive and backward-compatible.
- **Reduced-motion and replay/test paths:** The reduced-motion (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`) and replay paths must remain functional; the fix must not depend on animations having run.
- **Licensing:** All code/assets remain permissively licensed (MIT/Apache/CC0).
- **Scope:** Fix the selection/move reliability bug; do not add a hint-system overhaul or change game rules.

## Existing State

- **Selection logic:** `BeleagueredCastleScene.handleCardClick()` → `selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` implement click-to-select. `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.makeDraggable()` attaches the top card's `pointerdown` → `onCardClick`, and registers the top card as a draggable via the shared `DragDropManager.registerDraggable()`.
- **Interaction gate:** `interactionBlocked` returns true while `!dealComplete || gameEnded || autoCompleting`; `dealComplete` is set in the renderer's `onDealComplete`, which then calls `makeDraggable()`.
- **Registration race (confirmed):** Immediately after `makeDraggable()`, the top-card sprites are present in `scene.input` as interactive but sit in the input plugin's pending-insertion queue (`_pendingInsertion`) and are **not** yet in the active hit-test list (`_list`). A click arriving before the next input `preUpdate` is silently ignored. Diagnostic evidence: `sprite.input=true`, `input.enabled=true`, `inList=false`, `inPending=true`; the first click failed in 3 of 5 natural boots, while a retry (or a ≥~500 ms settle delay) always succeeded.
- **Renderer highlight:** `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` use raw `setTint()` / `clearTint()`. Per the `HandView` documentation, `setTint()` is a no-op in Phaser 4's Canvas renderer, so no selection highlight is visible when the game falls back to Canvas.
- **Only top cards interactive:** Covered (non-top) tableau cards are not interactive by design; clicking them does nothing. This is intentional but may read as "cannot select" to a new player.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` covers drag-to-foundation/tableau, illegal/out-of-zone snap-back, reduced-motion behaviour, and a click-vs-drag coexistence test (`click without drag still selects a column`). That suite boots in reduced-motion test mode (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`) and does not exercise the natural deal-then-click timing, which is where the race manifests.
- **Deployment:** The game uses `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with Canvas fallback) via `createCardGame`. `origin/main` and `dev` are functionally identical for BC input handling (differences are import-alias refactors and `GAME_INFO` metadata).

## Desired Change

1. **Eliminate the post-deal click race** so the first click after the deal always selects. Investigate the correct fix at the shared layer — e.g. ensure newly registered draggables/interactive top cards are flushed into the input hit-test list (or registered earlier / re-registered on the next tick) before interaction is considered available — rather than masking it with a game-local delay. Keep the fix additive and safe for all `DragDropManager`/`HandView` consumers.
2. **Make selection feedback renderer-agnostic:** replace BC's raw `setTint()` selection highlight with the shared Canvas-compatible mechanism (e.g. HandView's tint-overlay helper) or an equivalent persistent outline that renders in both WebGL and Canvas.
3. **Add natural-flow regression tests:** a browser test that boots without `__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`, dismisses the variant popup, waits for the deal, and asserts the immediate first click selects; plus a click-to-move end-to-end assertion. Reuse the existing BC drag-test helpers where possible.
4. **Verify the end-to-end contract** (select → destination click → one undoable move) and document the interaction as tested.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts` — `makeDraggable()` registration timing; `selectColumn()`/`deselectColumn()` highlight mechanism.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts` — `handleCardClick()`, `selectColumn()`, `wireInput()`, `interactionBlocked`, deal-complete wiring.
- `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` — `registerDraggable()` `setInteractive` / input-list timing; potential shared-layer fix.
- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — Canvas-compatible tint-overlay helper to reuse for BC selection.
- `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` — extend/add natural-flow first-click + click-to-move regression tests.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/help-content.json` — update only if the interaction contract changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Narrow-window vs persistent symptom:** The confirmed first-click race is short-lived (one input `preUpdate`); on a foregrounded 60 fps browser it is ~16 ms. The operator's "cannot select any cards" may be a broader symptom (perception, device, throttled frames, Canvas fallback). Mitigation: fix the confirmed defect, harden highlight visibility, and add an explicit open question for the operator; treat any additional scenario as a linked follow-up rather than expanding this item indefinitely.
- **Shared-module regression:** Changing `DragDropManager`/`HandView` input timing could affect Main Street, Golf, Coloretto and the Gym. Mitigation: keep the change additive, run the affected games' browser suites, and prefer a fix that does not alter existing drag semantics.
- **Test flakiness:** Timing-based browser tests can flake. Mitigation: assert on deterministic scene state (`selectedCol`, `moveCount`) and repeat the boot sequence across seeds; avoid wall-clock sleeps where possible.
- **Canvas fallback coverage:** Headless CI can force Canvas; verify the highlight fix visually/structurally in both renderer modes.
- **Scope creep:** A broader "make every card clickable" or "rework selection UX" redesign would expand scope. Record such ideas as linked follow-up work items instead.

### Assumptions
- The operator is running the current `dev` code in a standard browser (mouse input); the deployed `main` build is functionally identical for BC input.
- The first-click race is a genuine defect worth fixing regardless of whether it fully explains the operator's report.
- Reduced-motion and replay modes must remain unaffected by the fix.

## Related Work

- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [completed]: The epic that built the game, including click-to-move, drag-and-drop, undo/redo, and auto-move.
- **Click-to-Move Card Input (CG-0MLTFE68N1TONFIE)** [completed]: Introduced the click-to-move interaction contract this bug affects.
- **Highlight for selected card (CG-0MOJ44AXO006HFAS)** [completed]: Prior critical selection-feedback bug (market cards); establishes the project's expectation of a persistent, visible selection marker and Canvas-safe rendering.
- **Refactor Beleaguered Castle to use the core-engine drag-drop module (CG-0MSKSLDXQ008F5Y3)** [completed]: Moved BC onto the shared `DragDropManager` where the registration timing originates.
- **Add drag-drop browser tests for Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MSN4C4LI007VVGK)** [completed]: The existing BC interaction test suite that will be extended.
- **Reusable core-engine drag-drop module (CG-0MSKT0NQP0018KK6)** [completed]: The shared module whose `registerDraggable()` timing is implicated.
- **Bugs in Beleaguered Castle HandView/PileView migration** (related completed items under the BC epic) — context on recent BC interaction refactors.

### Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog and repository files for keywords derived from the report (beleaguered, castle, cards, click, deal, first, select, move, ignored, cannot). The automated `find-related` pass returned 3 related items and 3 repository matches:

- **CG-0MLTFCTNK10RQ41T** – Beleaguered Castle Game Logic (completed): the game-logic foundation underlying move legality used by selection/move.
- **CG-0MSRGV53I009BKKR** – Held-event play burst feedback (completed): interaction-feedback precedent in the codebase.
- **CG-0MUF6LBW600657B2** – [test-failure] skills-extensions-tracking.test.ts ignore check is vacuous (open): unrelated test-infrastructure item surfaced by keyword overlap; no dependency.
- Repository file matches: `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only — no code paths implicated).

The manual Related Work list above is the authoritative set; the automated matches are broad and mostly keyword-driven.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does the failure happen on the very first click after the deal, or on every click?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Investigation could only reproduce a *first-click-after-deal* drop; subsequent clicks succeeded. Awaiting operator confirmation of whether their experience is intermittent (first click) or total (all clicks).
- **Q: Are you playing in WebGL or does your browser fall back to Canvas?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Canvas fallback would additionally hide the `setTint` selection highlight, which could read as "not selected". The game defaults to `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL preferred).
- **Q: Is this the local dev build or the deployed `main` build?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). `main` and `dev` are functionally identical for BC input handling, so the same defect is expected in both.
- **Q: Are you clicking the fully visible top card of a column, or a partly covered card?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Only the top card of each column is interactive by design; covered cards intentionally do nothing.

## Suggested Next Step

Confirm the operator's exact scenario via the open questions above, then implement the confirmed fix (input-registration flush + Canvas-safe selection highlight) with natural-flow browser regression tests.
data.title: Beleaguered Castle: cards cannot be selected to move them (first click after deal ignored)

## Goal

Make every event card's coin/reputation text equal its current integer `card-data.csv` value so the text states the amount the engine actually applies (AC1).

## Context

Producer decision (OPEN QUESTION 1, answer A): `text = data`. 43 events are a plain ×100 rescale; 19 events have pre-existing rebalance drift and must be set to the current data value; 9 percent/duration/no-effect events are unchanged. Data columns must not change (no rebalancing).

## Acceptance Criteria

## Goal

Keep the committed card-face SVG artifacts and CSV checksum in sync with the corrected `card-data.csv` (AC4).

## Context

`card-svg-coverage.test.ts` regenerates the SVGs during the unit suite, and the generator writes `csv-checksum.json`; a stale committed checksum dirties the working tree and invalidates the read-only test cache. The generator emits only name, trigger, cost, `ongoingCost` and hand-slot text — no `description`/`effect` text — so no visual change is expected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Confirmed and documented that the SVGs contain no `description`/`effect` text (so the text corrections produce no SVG content change; only the checksum changes).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-coverage.test.ts` passes.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — regeneration entry point.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — regenerated artifacts.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — refreshed checksum.

**Deliverables:**

# Task: Verify fresh remote clones — game repos and launcher presets

## Goal

As a game developer, a fresh clone of a published game repo (with the engine
pulled in through the `core` submodule) installs, builds and unit-tests
successfully; and as a distribution builder the launcher can compose a subset of
the remote repos as siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a clean temporary directory,
   `git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git`
   followed by `npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`
   succeeds.
2. The same sequence succeeds for `tce-main-street` (parent AC3).
3. A fresh clone of `tableau-card-engine-core` succeeds and
   `npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit` passes inside
   it.
4. The launcher composes a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings against
   fresh clones: `GAMES_CONFIG=solo` and `GAMES_CONFIG=full` builds
   (`npm run build`) both succeed (parent AC4).
5. The exact commands executed and their outcomes are recorded on the parent
   work item as verification evidence; any failure is triaged into a critical
   `test-failure` work item rather than worked around.

## Minimal Implementation

- Clone into a clean temp directory (never reuse a prior checkout) so the
  submodule resolution on clone is genuinely exercised.
- Run the clone/build/test sequence for golf and main-street, plus core.
- For the launcher presets, clone the remote game repos as siblings under the
  paths the presets reference (`../tce-<game>`) and build with `GAMES_CONFIG`
  set to `solo` then `full`.
- Record failures with the exact command and output before triaging.

**Key Files:**

- `configs/solo.json` — the one-game preset spot check.
- `configs/full.json` — the all-games preset spot check.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — sibling-repo discovery used by the
  presets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — the documented clone/build/test workflow under test.

**Dependencies:**

**C4** (the repositories must exist and be pushed before a fresh clone can be
verified).

**Deliverables:**

- Fresh-clone verification evidence for golf, main-street, core and the
  `solo`/`full` launcher presets, recorded on the parent.
data.title: Verify fresh remote clones: game repos and launcher presets

## Problem

`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines the `unit` test type as:

```
npx tsx scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project unit --timeout-ms 300000 --reporter=default --reporter=./scripts/vitest-tap-reporter.ts
```

This omits `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, which the project's own test runners default to (`scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `run-dev-tests.sh`, `run-smoke-tests.sh`, `run-tutorial-tests.sh` all `export GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"`). As a result a bare `/skill:test --type unit` fails 4 tests in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` with:

```
Error: Could not auto-detect game type from transcript. Available adapters: none. Use --game <type> to specify explicitly.
```

Confirmed 2026-09-26 at dev `8b57d931`: bare `--project unit` exit 1 (4 failed / 7216 passed); with `GAMES_CONFIG=full` exit 0 (418 files / 7220 passed / 8 skipped).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `unit` command in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` sets `GAMES_CONFIG=full` (or otherwise ensures the game-discovery adapters load), consistent with the project test scripts.
2. A bare `/skill:test --type unit` (or the equivalent invocation) passes with 0 failures.
3. `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (skill-integrated test profiles section) and `AGENTS.md` reflect the corrected command.

## Notes

- Discovered during the audit of `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0`.
- Only the `unit` type was observed to be affected; verify `smoke`/`dev`/`browser`/`tutorial` similarly while fixing.
data.title: Fix /skill:test --type unit extension command to set GAMES_CONFIG=full
